transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. The suction through the hose points away from the main suction motor. The likely fault is in the floorhead/brush drive: most commonly hair or thread has jammed the roller, or the rubber drive belt has slipped, stretched or failed. A separate brush motor is the next possibility. 1. Turn the floorhead over. Remove hair and thread from around the roller and both ends. Try turning the roller by hand. If it is stiff or seized, that supports a jammed/worn brush bar.
2. If the base plate can be removed normally, inspect the belt. A snapped belt, one off the pulley, or one that looks glazed/stretched supports a belt failure. These checks can identify the cause, but they do not make the vacuum safe to run after a burning smell. If the roller and belt look intact, the floorhead brush motor or its thermal protection is more likely, which is an engineer repair.

ok unplugged n turned it over. brushbar turns by hand but was tight, loads of hair n a bit of tassel wrapped round the ends. cut it all off n it spins free now. took the plate off and the belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit has a shiny melted lookin edge. no sparks or electrical smell btw, just the rubber smell when it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The snapped belt is the clear cause of the brush bar stopping. The hair and tassel had made the roller tight, so the belt has slipped and overheated until it broke; the shiny melted edge and rubber smell fit that pattern. The brush bar now turning freely is encouraging, but because there was a burning smell, do not use the vacuum again or fit a belt and test it yourself. It needs a qualified engineer to inspect the brush-bar ends and belt drive for heat damage or remaining binding, then fit the correct belt if all is sound. The main suction motor is less likely to be the issue because suction through the hose remains present; this is concentrated around the floorhead brush drive.

candidates: Brush bar jammed with hair/thread, overloading the drive (high)
Fault in the floorhead brush-drive motor (medium)
